question: True or false: air at a 2,500 m training camp contains a smaller percentage of oxygen than air at sea level?
answer: False. Oxygen makes up about 20.9% of dry air at any height athletes train at. What falls is the pressure: at 2,500 m it is about three quarters of sea level, so each breath carries fewer molecules of everything. Altitude tents work the other way, removing oxygen to mimic the same shortage.
move: Separate how much of the mixture is there from how much mixture there is.
trap: Assuming thin air means air with less oxygen in the mix.

diagram.caption: Oxygen is 20.9% of the air at both; each breath simply holds a quarter fewer molecules.

source: West, Schoene & Milledge, High Altitude Medicine, 2007
reference: West, Schoene & Milledge, High Altitude Medicine and Physiology, Hodder Arnold, 2007
